description:
Hi team,

I am seeking some advice regarding Teams meetings.

I am organising the Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) meeting scheduled for 11 September. The Executive Boardroom (Kookaburra Room - 50 MC), has been booked through our group mailbox, AuditandRiskSecretariat@education.gov.au<mailto:AuditandRiskSecretariat@education.gov.au>.

When setting up the meeting invitation, I attempted to add a Teams link and assign co-organisers. However, it appears that I am unable to add co-organisers when creating the meeting from the group mailbox, which means I cannot grant me and my team the ability to manage the meeting.

From my reading online, it appears I may need to create the Teams meeting from my personal email account, invite the Boardroom and then copy the Teams link into the invitation sent from the ARC group mailbox to attendees.

Could you please confirm whether this is the correct approach, or advise if there is another way to add co-organisers when scheduling a Teams meeting from a shared mailbox?

Thanks
Claudia

short_description: For Advice: Overseas Joining Microsoft Teams Issue
description:
Location:  Level 10, 108 Wakefield Street, ADELAIDE SA 5000
Contact number: (02) 6240 9173


Hello Service desk,

I'm seeking some advice regarding external participants joining Microsoft Teams meetings from overseas.

We recently had two Youth Advisory Group members experience issues accessing a Microsoft Teams meeting while travelling overseas. One participant was located in China and advised they were using a VPN, which appeared to be functioning correctly for other applications and services, however they were unable to join the meeting. The attached screenshot shows the error message they received:
"The account you're using doesn't have access to this meeting due to org policies. Please join without using an account."


We also had another participant experience difficulties joining from Italy, with the link not working and them getting this error message:
[cid:image002.jpg@01DD2373.35B41B30]

We have another Youth Advisory Group meeting scheduled for Wednesday, with a participant intending to join from Portugal, and we're hoping to understand whether they may encounter similar issues and whether there are any steps we can take in advance to support their participation.

Could you please advise whether there are any known restrictions, organisational policy settings, or overseas access limitations that may affect external participants joining Microsoft Teams meetings from overseas, particularly when using personal devices or non-government accounts?

For further context, we have had Youth Advisory Group members join Microsoft Teams meetings from overseas in the past without experiencing any issues. As this appears to be a new challenge, we're trying to understand whether there are any specific settings, restrictions or location-based considerations that may have contributed to these participants being unable to access the meeting.

I've attached the screenshots provided by one of the participants for reference.

Many thanks,
Sam

The Process

  1.  All returns require the Provider to complete and submit a Records Register, identifying what will be returned to the department (in physical or digital format)



  1.  Once we have confirmed the Record register is completed it will be accepted and the IM Team will:


·       provide a Secure File Transfer Portal (SFTP) link to transfer the digital files. The department might provide additional instructions depending on what information is in the spreadsheet.  Once we have confirmed import of the information we will inform you and you can tell the provider to delete their copy.

·       Organise boxes and barcodes to be sent directly to the Provider so physical information can be boxed for transfer.  Once affixed to the boxes the barcodes must be added to the register so that the files can be identified within each box.  Once this is sent and accepted by the department the Provider can (at their cost) organise transfer to the closest repository for our storage provider. The address will be provided at this point in the process.



Completing the Register

We require completion of the attached (or a similar system extract) register for digital records.  This enables us to confirm which records we can expect to be returned as part of the transfer process.

20634 - records documenting the assessment of higher education, post-secondary and technical and vocational qualifications from overseas. Destroy 75 years after date of birth of applicant or 7 years after last action, whichever is later



20635 - Records documenting: management of programs and schemes - legacy records of copies of examination papers, examination results and statistical summaries of exam results, administrative arrangements for examinations and examination case files related to this function. Destroy 10 years after last action



This determines how long the record needs to be kept.  This will need to be applied to the relevant records on the register.



The disposal date is the date the record is due for destruction based on the last action on the file.

  1.  this will be a date in the past for records already destroyed


  1.  this will be a date in the future for records that have not yet met the minimum retention requirements and are being sent to the department.

short_description: USB Port Blockers for HP OfficeJet 250 Mobile All-in-one printers
description:
Hi Brad,

Thank you for advising us of the scanning functionality currently available on the HP OfficeJet 250 Mobile All-in-One printers.

We understand that three exemptions have been approved for remote printing, with HP OfficeJet 250 printers provisioned for Minister Clare's Office, Minister Rishworth's Office, and the Education Intergovernmental Team. These exemptions apply to printing only and do not extend to scanning.

The 'scan to USB' capability introduces an additional risk, as it allows information to be saved to unencrypted removable media. We are unable to mitigate this risk through device configuration as there is no administrative setting available to disable the USB port or selectively disable the 'scan to USB' function.

To address this risk, could we please proceed with the purchase and installation of USB port blockers for these printers to prevent use of the 'scan to USB' capability.

Products such as the the Lindy USB Type-A Port Blocker<https://www.lindy.com.au/usb-port-blocker-4-pack-key-blue?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=22809137167&gclid=EAIaIQobChMI-fSKrsTllQMVYM1MAh2cjBsIEAQYASABEgL3KvD_BwE> provide a simple, practical, and cost-effective way (approx. $20 each) to restrict access to the USB ports and prevent the use of removable media.

Thank you for your assistance in implementing this control. Please let me know if you have any questions.

Kind regards,

The CDDA Scheme provides a mechanism for the department to compensate individuals who have experienced detriment (i.e. quantifiable financial loss) due to defective administration, and who have no other avenue of redress.

The application relates to Mr Alexander Petrovic (the 'claimant'),  jobseeker ID is 2998424609. The claimant received services from an employment services provider, Jobfind Cheltenham (Jobfind) between 2008-2009. These services were likely delivered under the Job Network Program.

The claimant has provided further information in relation to his claim, and we would appreciate your assistance with providing further background information from this time.

Context

The claimant alleges:


  *   The employment services provider, Jobfind, engaged in misconduct towards him in early November 2008. The claimant alleges he called the Department via telephone to report the misconduct in early November 2008; and
  *   Jobfind did not assist him with searching for and obtaining employment.

Request

We would appreciate your assistance to search and provide any of the following records (if they exist):


  *   Any records of correspondence with, and complaints made by, the claimant to the Department in November 2008, including any investigation records or reports
  *   Any records of the claimant's appointment history with JobFind between 2008-09, including Jobfind case notes

Hi Lokesh,



I have completed the review based on the case details and the documentation shared by @Damien Villaret<mailto:Damien.Villaret@qlik.com>. Based on the evidence available, the most likely root cause appears to be related to the Windows Defender configuration, RabbitMQ log behaviour and the way the NPrinting services are interacting with the underlying file system.



The intermittent Scheduler crashes along with the associated On-Demand hangs and occasional user lockouts are consistent with RabbitMQ losing access to its data files while performing write operations. RabbitMQ is the messaging component used by the NPrinting Scheduler and Engine services for On-Demand processing and task coordination. The failure pattern is recurring and shows the same signature each time: an Erlang {badmatch,{error,eacces}} exception against the persistent message store in RabbitMQ's data directory under  C:\ProgramData\NPrinting\RabbitMQ\db\. The eacces error indicates an access-denied condition at the operating system level, which strongly suggests third-party interference while the files are being written.



From the Defender configuration-change history reviewed for the period 18 June to 16 July, no exclusion appears to have been configured for the RabbitMQ or NPrinting data directories on this host. This aligns with the repeated crash pattern observed since mid-June, as well as the timestamps captured in the AirLock logs.



This issue is separate from the earlier Attack Surface Reduction rule problem that was blocking Qlik.NPrinting.Scheduler.exe under the "Block credential stealing from lsass.exe" policy. That earlier issue appears to have stopped recurring after 10 July. While the exact reason for that change is not fully confirmed, it is not related to the RabbitMQ access-denied crashes, which have continued independently through 13-15 July.



Recommended immediate actions are as follows:

  *   Follow up on the exclusion request that has already been raised with the central Defender/CIS policy team. The requested exclusions include:
     *   Folder exclusion: C:\ProgramData\NPrinting\RabbitMQ
     *   Process exclusions: erl.exe, epmd.exe, Qlik.NPrinting.Scheduler.exe
  *   Treat this as a high-priority item, as it is likely to resolve the crash mechanism identified above.
  *   Perform a controlled validation by temporarily pausing AirLock scanning on this host for 24-48 hours to determine whether the hang/crash frequency decreases. This will help confirm whether Defender, AirLock, or both are contributing to the issue.



At this stage, there is no evidence pointing to a defect in the NPrinting product itself. The issue also does not appear to be related to the May 2026 upgrade as the same pattern predates it. Once the exclusions are correctly applied and validated, I expect the issue to be resolved.



I am available to join a call with the customers IT team to provide any additional technical clarification required and to discuss the findings in more detail. @Damien Villaret<mailto:Damien.Villaret@qlik.com> Please let me know if you have any call/meeting setup with them for next week.

Hi Lokesh,



I have completed the review based on the case details and the documentation shared by @Damien Villaret<mailto:Damien.Villaret@qlik.com>. Based on the evidence available, the most likely root cause appears to be related to the Windows Defender configuration, RabbitMQ log behaviour and the way the NPrinting services are interacting with the underlying file system.



The intermittent Scheduler crashes along with the associated On-Demand hangs and occasional user lockouts are consistent with RabbitMQ losing access to its data files while performing write operations. RabbitMQ is the messaging component used by the NPrinting Scheduler and Engine services for On-Demand processing and task coordination. The failure pattern is recurring and shows the same signature each time: an Erlang {badmatch,{error,eacces}} exception against the persistent message store in RabbitMQ's data directory under  C:\ProgramData\NPrinting\RabbitMQ\db\. The eacces error indicates an access-denied condition at the operating system level, which strongly suggests third-party interference while the files are being written.



From the Defender configuration-change history reviewed for the period 18 June to 16 July, no exclusion appears to have been configured for the RabbitMQ or NPrinting data directories on this host. This aligns with the repeated crash pattern observed since mid-June, as well as the timestamps captured in the AirLock logs.



This issue is separate from the earlier Attack Surface Reduction rule problem that was blocking Qlik.NPrinting.Scheduler.exe under the "Block credential stealing from lsass.exe" policy. That earlier issue appears to have stopped recurring after 10 July. While the exact reason for that change is not fully confirmed, it is not related to the RabbitMQ access-denied crashes, which have continued independently through 13-15 July.



Recommended immediate actions are as follows:

  *   Follow up on the exclusion request that has already been raised with the central Defender/CIS policy team. The requested exclusions include:
     *   Folder exclusion: C:\ProgramData\NPrinting\RabbitMQ
     *   Process exclusions: erl.exe, epmd.exe, Qlik.NPrinting.Scheduler.exe
  *   Treat this as a high-priority item, as it is likely to resolve the crash mechanism identified above.
  *   Perform a controlled validation by temporarily pausing AirLock scanning on this host for 24-48 hours to determine whether the hang/crash frequency decreases. This will help confirm whether Defender, AirLock, or both are contributing to the issue.



At this stage, there is no evidence pointing to a defect in the NPrinting product itself. The issue also does not appear to be related to the May 2026 upgrade as the same pattern predates it. Once the exclusions are correctly applied and validated, I expect the issue to be resolved.



I am available to join a call with the customers IT team to provide any additional technical clarification required and to discuss the findings in more detail. @Damien Villaret<mailto:Damien.Villaret@qlik.com> Please let me know if you have any call/meeting setup with them for next week.

short_description: Clarification on Server Certificate Requirements for Authentication / mTLS
description:
Hello IT Security Team,

I am seeking clarification regarding departmental requirements for server certificates and authentication.

As part of an investigation into potential mTLS requirements for ENET application servers, I reviewed several Windows servers and found that:

1. Some servers have certificates installed in the Local Computer certificate store.
Where present, the certificates are typically issued to either the server hostname or the URL of a web application hosted on the server.
2. These certificates include an associated private key.
3. Not all servers reviewed have a certificate installed.

Could you advise whether there is an existing security policy, standard, or architectural requirement that mandates all servers to have a certificate installed that can be used for server authentication? 

If there is currently no policy or mandate requiring server authentication certificates on all servers, are there any planned security initiatives, roadmap items, or architectural standards that may introduce such a requirement in the future?

Regards,
Elvis

I wanted to raise an issue with the current recurring SEM meeting invitation and suggest a possible solution.

We concluded with my suggestion - that each rostered division issue the recurring SEM meeting invitation for the period that they are acting as Secretariat.

This approach would:

  *   Reduce the risk of issues associated with the long-standing recurring meeting series;
  *   Ensure the current Secretariat has ownership of the meeting details and attendee management during their roster period; and

short_description: FWO SharePoint site summary request and connection to Castlepoint
description:
Hello DEWR SharePoint Solutions Team,

We are seeking to initiate the process of establishing connections between FWO SharePoint sites and Castlepoint.

As Castlepoint is currently unable to automatically discover and connect SharePoint sites in our environment, a manual process is required to identify and progressively establish connections.

As a first step, could you please provide a report of current FWO SharePoint sites that are not exempt from the retention policy, including any relevant site details that would assist in determining connection scope?
Following receipt of the report, we propose to:

  1.  Review the identified SharePoint sites.
  2.  Compare the report against the list of SharePoint sites already connected to Castlepoint.
  3.  Identify sites that remain in scope for connection.
  4.  Provide the resulting list to the SharePoint Solutions team and request assistance to establish the required Castlepoint connections.

Could you please advise whether there are any additional steps required from your perspective, or whether there are any other teams that we should engage with as part of this process to establish these connections?

short_description: RE: IT access for our posted Minister Counsellor
description:
Good morning, Liz,

Thanks for reaching out. Looking into your request, I would agree that RAS or GovTEAMS would work. Both options provide access to Microsoft Teams and other Microsoft 365 tools including SharePoint accessibility. GovTEAMS promotes easy collaboration for local, national, and international users up to Sensitive or PROTECTED environments. With the inclusion of a SharePoint you'll have a shared access storage space that will suit your requirements for collaborative document editing, commenting and tracked changes. It can also double as a workspace to assist with maintaining and organising briefing materials.

A few things to note regarding GovTEAMS.

1. GovTEAMS is fully managed by the Department of Finance and they have they own support structure.
2. GovTEAMS (official and protected) attracts a subscription fee which will be funded from your projects/division budget.
3. Any information maintained on this platform is not owned by the department.

They unfortunately don't have a direct contact number, and it's suggested to reach out with enquiries through their online contact form. I've attached it below.

Contact us | The collaboration service for the Australian Public Service | GovTEAMS<https://www.govteams.gov.au/contact-us>

Please also see the following knowledge base article covering some information on GovTEAMS - Corporate - ICT Services - GovTEAMS - Collaboration Website (Whole of Government)<https://dese.service-now.com/servicedeskportal?id=kb_article_view&sys_kb_id=dc46448e83597e9052b971426daad301&table=kb_knowledge&searchTerm=govteams>

Looking at RAS as the next option I believe the staff in question already have existing DEWR accounts with RAS access. Our systems show that Tara Williams has an existing RAS Cloud PC. The regular process for users looking to enter our environment virtually is using their DEWR account from a DFAT or personal device and connect via Windows365. As this is already in place and provides access to Teams, SharePoint and another collaboration tools within our environment they would just need to request specific accesses or be provided access to specific documents or SharePoint pages.

If you're looking to include the locally engaged staff members in Geneva, we advise pursuing GovTEAMS as those staff do not have a DEWR accounts.

Happy to answer any more questions or discuss further when you are free either Wednesday or Thursday.

Thank you,

Kieran Hayes

short_description: [for TSD Linux admin team] Error Publishing to Connect
description:
Hi Teams.
                   One of the Developers has sent through this. Can you please help have a look: 

=======================================================================


During deployment, the curl package fails to install. From the logs, it appears the deployment environment is using an older version of libcurl, which may be causing compatibility issues with the current version of the R curl package.

The relevant error messages are:

Local libcurl is too old. Downloading a static libcurl for legacy Linux...

followed by:

handle.c:426:8: error: 'CURL_HTTP_VERSION_3' undeclared
handle.c:489:51: error: 'CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_METHOD' undeclared
ERROR: compilation failed for package 'curl'

As a result, the deployment process is unable to complete successfully.

This issue appears to be new, as I have not encountered it previously and it seems separate from last week's problem.

I've attached a screenshot of the deployment log for reference.
 

Could you please investigate whether there have been any recent changes to the publishing environment, or whether the server's libcurl version may need updating?

short_description: RE: IT access for our posted Minister Counsellor
description:
Hi Service Desk,

I am seeking advice on potential digital collaboration solutions for our team.

Our team supports Tara Williams (Minister Counsellor) and a locally engaged staff member based in Geneva. They operate within the DFAT ICT environment, while our team is based in DEWR. As a result, our collaboration is currently limited primarily to email and document attachments.

We support them across a broad range of International Labour Organization (ILO) matters, including providing briefing and instructions during ILO sessions. We are also looking to strengthen our ability to share information and collaborate on ILO-related work throughout the year, including maintaining briefing materials, background information and work in progress between sessions.

We are interested in understanding whether there are approved options that would allow collaboration across the DEWR and DFAT environments, including:

  *   shared document storage
  *   collaborative document editing, comments and tracked changes
  *   a shared workspace for maintaining briefing materials and background information
  *   dashboard-style visibility of work items and priorities, and
  *   appropriate security and access controls.

Potential options we have considered include:

  *   RAS access for Geneva-based staff to the DEWR environment
  *   GovTEAMS
  *   Microsoft Teams, SharePoint or other Microsoft 365 collaboration tools, and
  *   any other approved cross-agency collaboration solutions.

I understand there may be security and interoperability constraints given the different departmental networks. However, I would appreciate advice on what options are available, and whether there are any established approaches used to support collaboration with officers posted overseas and operating within another agency's ICT environment.

I am very happy to set up a time to discuss. If there is someone free on Wednesday or Thursday this week, please let me know and I'll send through a meeting request.

Many thanks,

Liz Leiter

short_description: Power BI Dataflow Gen1 Legacy Classification and Dataflow Gen2 Access
description:
Hi Team,

We have noticed that Power BI Dataflow Gen1 is now classified as a legacy feature, and that Dataflow Gen2 is not currently accessible to us. We experienced a similar situation last year with DataMart, which were retired by Microsoft, requiring us to redesign our solution after a significant amount of work had already been completed. As Fabric-related features were not available to us at the time, we were left without an equivalent replacement solution for approximately 10 months and had to develop a workaround to carry on with our operational work.

As we are currently undertaking a substantial data reform project, we would like to understand the implications of any future retirement or removal of Dataflow Gen1. Specifically, if Dataflow Gen1 is retired, will existing Dataflows be automatically migrated to Dataflow Gen2, or will a manual migration be required?

We are keen to avoid a situation where we need to rebuild the entire solution from scratch and would appreciate any guidance or confirmation you can obtain from Microsoft regarding the migration path and associated impacts.

Thanks in advance for your assistance.

Regards,
Vignesh

short_description: Positive Partnerships Program - Information Management Advice
description:
Good afternoon,

Our team manages the longstanding Positive Partnerships program, which delivers workshops, training and other resources for parents, carers, teachers and other school staff of Autistic school-aged students, under a services contract. We're reaching out to seek your advice on the program's information management, and our obligations under the Archives Act.

We recently conducted an Open Tender for Phase 5 of the program, and the incumbent supplier was selected to deliver the Phase from 1 July 2026. We are currently in a transition period, as we roll-out the new Phase, and wind-down Phase 4. This includes an uplift of the program website, services and handover of Phase 4 data and materials.

To support program delivery, the supplier collects information on our behalf, such as details for participant registration, feedback and evaluation. Through the previous phase, this data has been stored by the supplier and shared with the department at an aggregate level, through reporting. Although, we are exploring greater visibility and departmental access in Phase 5. Noting that sensitive information is collected under the program, such as whether participants identify as First Nations, Culturally and Linguistically diverse or have children with an Autism diagnosis, we are also in contact with the Privacy team as we work through conducting a Privacy Impact Assessment.

As Phase 5 has a particular focus on strengthening performance monitoring and evaluation requirements, and ensuring there are robust data practices, we have consulted across our departments on the data and reporting requirements included in the Phase 5 contract. Through these consultations we have been advised that data collected for the program would likely be considered Commonwealth Record, although additional program management data such as staff records likely wouldn't be. As this data would fall under the archives act requirements, it was recommended that we reach out to your team for assistance in understanding these requirements and how they should apply to this program. In particular:

Phase 4:

Hi Prod DBAs, Gurdeep, as discussed could you please address the growth of SSISDB database in prod (AG1EMP_SSIS01.application.enet,14331).

The first issue is essentially a data discrepancy - SSIS log entries exist that are older than 6mths, and have no end-date populated.  This prevents the rows from being cleaned up by the internal purge process.

To address this we need to manually update the status of these logs (to complete or '1'), which allows the cleanup process to purge them.  However done in one go this resulted in the cleanup process running for 28min in the lower env (approx. 5minutes was a normal cleanup duration).  Therefore we probably need to do this in an incremental way - such as addressing 10% of the defunct logs, running the cleanup process, and repeating until all defunct rows are purged.

The attached '03_update_stale_logging.sql' script performs this in increments of (10) log entries (a log entry parent can have thousands of rows in fk tables).


The second task is to reduce the configured retention period in SSISDB.  We have decided that 3mths retention is sufficient for our production support requirements. Subject: Inbox Access for Rebecca O'Neill [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Dear Marcel

To enable Bec to assist you with EA functions, could you please provide your written return approval to allow her "full" access to you Inbox:

Mailbox access
Your EA will need to be granted Full Access permission in Microsoft Exchange, if you would like them to access Outlook features such as:
*       your Online Archive,
*       your Out of Office notifications, and/or
*       access to your mailbox via Outlook for iOS on an Intune device,
To do this, please send an email to servicedesk@dewr.gov.au<mailto:servicedesk@dewr.gov.au> outlining that you are willing to give Full Access to your mailbox. The Service Desk can only give Full Access to the mailbox and cannot give access to specific folders (such as your Inbox).
The Service Desk will apply these permissions within the Microsoft Exchange system. Once the permissions have been applied, it will automatically add the mailbox to the EA's Outlook. They will have full visibility of your mailbox, calendar and settings.
*Please note that if your EA has previously added your mailbox through other means, it will need to be removed from their Outlook prior to making this request, as it may cause a sync issue.
Send on behalf permission
If you would like your EA to send mail on your behalf, please include this instruction in your email to servicedesk@dewr.gov.au<mailto:servicedesk@dewr.gov.au>. With this permission, emails sent by your EA will show they are sent on your behalf in the sender details.

If you would prefer "restricted" access, please let me know:

Granting access to specific email folders
If you wish to grant access to specific folders in the Outlook desktop app only, please follow the instructions below.
The top-level mail folder
This is the folder (above your Inbox) that every other folder sits in; e.g. Inbox, Sent Items, Deleted Items etc. Depending on which version of Outlook you're using, the top-level folder could be identified by either your name, or your email address,
1.      Right-click on the folder, then click Data File Properties -> Permissions tab.
2.      Add their name, then ensure Folder Visible is checked.
Without this access, they won't be able to view any other folders in your mailbox.
Inbox
1.      Right-click on the folder, then click Properties -> Permissions tab.
2.      Add their name, and select an appropriate Permission Level from the drop-down, such as Editor.
Sent Items
1.      Right-click on the folder, then click Properties -> Permissions tab.
2.      Add their name, and select an appropriate permission level from the drop-down, such as Editor.
Without this access, any mail they send on your behalf won't be saved.
Deleted Items
1.      Right-click on the folder, then click Properties -> Permissions tab.
2.      Add their name, and select an appropriate permission level from the drop-down; such as Editor.
To be able to delete items (such as Calendar entries or emails) delegates require Editor permissions to their deleted items folder. Without this permission:
*       any mail your EA deletes will be permanently lost, and
*       your EA will be unable to delete any of your calendar entries,
By default, mail items are automatically removed from Deleted Items after 90 days.
Access to other specific folders or subfolders
*       Consider whether you want your EA to access any of your other mail folders.
*       Set access to each folder individually, using the same steps as above.

Kind regards

Lynley

	1. Power off the VSA Access Node (EPRIBKN347).
	2. Edit the .vmx file of the VSA Access Node:
	3. Update the SCSI Controller port assignments, as per the following:
			scsi0.pciSlotNumber = "160"
			scsi1.pciSlotNumber = "1184"
			scsi2.pciSlotNumber = "224"
			scsi3.pciSlotNumber = "256"
	4. Save the .vmx file and upload it back to the datastore.
	5. Power on the VSA Access Node

short_description: Installation of CHROME Extension Name: SAP CPI Helper on my System
description:
Business Case:

Extension Name:
SAP CPI Helper

Extension ID:
epoggeaemnknacpinjfgccbjakglngkpb

Business Justification:

I am currently working as an SAP Integration Suite (SAP CPI) developer supporting multiple CPI integration projects, including the enhancement of the eInvoicing interface for attachment processing and malware scanning, SNOW integration and S4C initiatives.

SAP CPI Helper is a widely used productivity extension for SAP CPI developers and provides usability enhancements for the SAP Integration Suite web interface. The extension does not create or modify integrations directly; rather, it improves visibility, troubleshooting, monitoring, and navigation capabilities that are already available within SAP Integration Suite.

Key benefits include:

• Improved trace analysis and troubleshooting of CPI messages.
• Direct navigation to message traces, logs, and attachments.
• Easier review of message payloads during development and testing.
• Faster diagnosis of integration issues and failed message processing.
• Improved productivity when supporting CPI interfaces in development, testing, and operational support activities.
• Better visibility of exchange properties, headers, and payload content during troubleshooting.
• Reduction in time spent manually navigating between CPI monitoring screens.

Current Use Case:

I am currently implementing and testing enhancements to the eInvoicing CPI interfaces, including attachment handling, malware scanning integration, XSLT mapping updates, and end-to-end message tracing. The SAP CPI Helper extension would significantly improve efficiency when reviewing message traces, payloads, attachments, and execution paths within CPI.

Business Benefit:

• Faster investigation and resolution of integration incidents.
• Reduced support effort and troubleshooting time.
• Improved productivity for CPI development and testing activities.
• Better visibility of message processing during project delivery and ongoing support.

The extension is only intended to support SAP Integration Suite (SAP CPI) development and troubleshooting activities and will be used solely for business-related work.

Thank you for considering this request.

TLS 1.2

TLS 1.0

  *   creation of a Microsoft List Form for a tracker

BACKGROUND:

  *   Quality is a sub-team of the People, Learning and Quality team<https://cd.hosts.application.enet/OrgUnit/Detail/50038420> in the Contact Centre
  *   They currently use a Microsoft List form tracker<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/DEWR-ContactCentresBranch-TEAM/Lists/Support%20Queue%20Tracker/AllItems.aspx?sortField=Created&isAscending=false&viewid=1c31f69f%2D9955%2D45d3%2D8435%2De6828e66fde1> (made in 2024 by previous knowledge management team) to track:
     *   calls to the call centres internal support queue
     *   escalation calls
     *   all quality assurance activities
  *   This tracker feeds into a PowerBI report managed by the data team (@Eeli Lee<mailto:EeLi.Lee@dewr.gov.au> and @DOLAN,Kate<mailto:Kate.Dolan@dewr.gov.au>) to provide a variety of quality assurance reports.

ISSUE

  1.  The Microsoft List form tracker<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/DEWR-ContactCentresBranch-TEAM/Lists/Support%20Queue%20Tracker/AllItems.aspx?sortField=Created&isAscending=false&viewid=1c31f69f%2D9955%2D45d3%2D8435%2De6828e66fde1> currently has around 52,000 entries which is causing lag and issue with the PowerBI report
  2.  The tracker is currently located on Contact Centres Branch SharePoint - Home<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/DEWR-ContactCentresBranch-TEAM/SitePages/Home1.aspx> managed by Knowledge Management (KM)
     *   Quality currently has to reach out to KM to give new staff access to the tracker
     *   KM would like Quality team to fully manage access to the tracker going forward

PROPOSED SOLUTION
After discussions, Quality, Data and Knowledge Management have come up with a solution:

  *   Quality team will request a new SharePoint site to be built via the Microsoft Teams Request<https://forms.microsoft.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=Ff0M3VhFEkuLreommE_EF0GlBi_s76lGhBW-vWcex6BUM0EzTVlXWEtaNEczOUEyUlo0UlhQS0JXSS4u> form

  *   A new Microsoft List form tracker<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/DEWR-ContactCentresBranch-TEAM/Lists/Support%20Queue%20Tracker/AllItems.aspx?sortField=Created&isAscending=false&viewid=1c31f69f%2D9955%2D45d3%2D8435%2De6828e66fde1> to be created
     *   It is planned a new tracker will be created yearly to ensure there is no lag
     *   There is understanding new trackers may need to be created more often if lag persists
     *   New tracker will be linked to PowerBI and data from old tracker to be included in the PowerBI

HELP REQUEST
Once the SharePoint site request is approved, can we ask for someone or a contact person from SharePoint solutions to help out with:

  *   Setting up the new Quality SharePoint site
     *   This includes walking through @RYAN,Casey<mailto:Casey.Ryan@dewr.gov.au> or other Quality leadership to set up members and accesses
  *   Setting up a new Microsoft List form
     *   Form will be a duplicate of the current one Microsoft List form tracker<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/DEWR-ContactCentresBranch-TEAM/Lists/Support%20Queue%20Tracker/AllItems.aspx?sortField=Created&isAscending=false&viewid=1c31f69f%2D9955%2D45d3%2D8435%2De6828e66fde1>
     *   Includes testing with data team (contact person: @Eeli Lee<mailto:EeLi.Lee@dewr.gov.au> or @DOLAN,Kate<mailto:Kate.Dolan@dewr.gov.au>) to test if new tracker will link to the existing PowerBI

Urgent Request: Replacement Teams Headset

I use a headset to participate in Microsoft Teams meetings at my desk and rely on all meeting audio being routed through the headset. Over the past month, the headset has become increasingly unreliable, with meeting audio frequently switching from the headset to the laptop speakers without warning.

While I can sometimes manually switch the audio back to the headset, on other occasions the audio continues to play through the laptop speakers. In an open plan office environment, this presents a significant confidentiality risk, particularly when sensitive or protected information is being discussed.

To manage the issue, I have had to leave my workstation and move into available meeting rooms whenever the headset fails and audio redirects to the laptop speakers. This is disruptive, impacts productivity, and is not a sustainable solution.

Given the ongoing reliability issues, the risk of inadvertent disclosure of confidential information, and the impact on my ability to participate in meetings effectively, I consider this matter to be urgent. The headset is no longer fit for purpose and requires replacement as soon as possible to mitigate the confidentiality and operational risks.

Good morning team,

Nik Parevski assisted our team earlier this year (INC0483451) by building on a PowerShell script that Chris Counsell had previously created for us, and we're hoping to utilise Nik's talents once again.

Earlier this year, the Cyber Assurance team advised that 7zip would be removed from laptops. The removal of 7zip's functionality would disrupt our process for receiving and importing employment service provider data into Content Manager where we are often required to unzip and extract data from hundreds or thousands of ZIP files, depending on how the provider has packaged the data.
We have confirmed that staff can submit a business case to request retain access to 7zip, however, this access is only temporary while we are expected to find a permanent solution. Unfortunately we have found that the standard Windows ZIP functionality does not allow you to unzip multiple ZIP files simultaneously, so we are currently seeking an alternative solution.


There are two main scenarios where we require assistance:

	1. Multiple standalone ZIP files
In most cases, we receive a large number of ZIP files sitting at the same directory level. Each of these ZIP files needs to be extracted into its own folder, retaining the original ZIP file name as the folder name (see 'Multiple Standalone ZIP Files' image).

Ideally, this will be achieved with a simple PowerShell script that unzips all ZIP files contained at the main directory level, with a window similar to our existing script that allows us to select the 'starting folder'.

	2. "Archiving [date]" ZIP files
We often receive data from a particular provider who transfers anywhere from 20 to 30+ ZIP files for a given archiving date (e.g. "Archiving 10?11?2025 SS5.zip", shown in the 'Archiving ZIP Files' image - attached).

Each of these "Archiving…" ZIP files contains multiple ZIP files for individual participants. Ideally, a script for this scenario would:
	• Pull the participant ZIP files from the parent "Archiving…" ZIP to the main directory level (i.e. where the 'Archiving…' ZIP files are located), and
	• Unzip each participant ZIP into its own folder, preserving the original ZIP file name for the folder.

This is the same process that Nik's script helped us with earlier this year (although it focused on the ZIP files within the participant files). 

If possible, it would be great to add these two steps to the start of that script; however, if it's easier or more appropriate to run these steps run as a separate script, we're happy to proceed that way. I have attached a txt file of the script that Nik made for us for reference.

short_description: Provider Payment Delay and Potential Ministerial Escalation Risk (CHG0079425)
description:
Hi team

Lodging this incident - A small provider has been awaiting payment for the past few months. A July Release code fix was implemented with the expectation that the issue would be resolved through the currently in-progress July 2026 pay run.

Business advised this morning that the provider may escalate the ongoing payment delay to the Minister, increasing the urgency of resolving this matter.

At present, we are unable to rerun processing to achieve the intended payment outcome for the current pay run. While a data fix remains a potential fallback remediation option, our preferred approach is to rerun the Linking Loan processing ahead of the scheduled pay run processing to deliver payment sooner.

However, this cannot occur until completion of the HITS database EDT migration activities under CHG0079425 (associated with HITS Release CHG007876), which include data ingestion and re-enablement of loan processing functionality. The change commenced late on 15/07/2026 and remains ongoing. Issues have been encountered with the HITS connection string and database connectivity, preventing completion of the migration activities.

The tech teams (Jigar Sheth (EDT), Mukhtar Ahmad (VSCL), Khan (Database Team), Brendan Ryan (EDT)) are actively investigating.

Current findings are:

  *   Connectivity from ADF to the Ops Server has been confirmed as operational.
  *   Investigation is currently focused on connectivity between the Ops Server and the new HITS database.

Hi EMT

I ran some diagnostics and hope this would help to resolve the issue.
I am not sure how this has happened on some random servers unless there was a network change such as VPC migration or a network routing change or a gateway change( Unlikely as they may not target specific Ips to allow or deny)

Following shows :
Local agent is running>> No Airlock or local issue: on ZDEEAPP239SB

[cid:image007.png@01DD15DC.6876AFA0]

Local defender inbound and outbound rules exists for port 443 and not a local FW block

[cid:image008.png@01DD15DC.6876AFA0]

The server outbound traffic can go through 443 to external traffic,  but not to dev.Azure.com
[cid:image009.png@01DD15DC.6876AFA0]


I found that the traffic was not going through proxy and then I added a session env variable to force routing via proxy and results are different -below:

[cid:image010.png@01DD15DC.6876AFA0]

This could be suspected as server routing or some changes on the  network .

Thanks
Don

description:

US import tariff changes








 Dear Karen,



We are writing to tell you about changes to the way United States import tariffs will be calculated for postal items sent from Australia to the US.

Outbound parcels to the US

US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has advised that the 10 per cent global tariffs on items being sent to the US will expire on 24 July 2026. Instead, customers will be charged on a per-Harmonised System Codes (HS Codes) and Country of Origin (COO) basis with the corresponding duty rate being a percentage of the declared value of the goods.

CBP also advised that customers will no longer have the option to apply 6 or 8-digit HS Codes on outbound parcels headed for the US from Australia. Effective 24 July 2026, CBP will only accept 10-digit HS Codes. Items without a 10-digit HS code may be returned.

HS Codes influence how the US calculates tariffs and duties on items being sent to the US. CBP can only apply tariffs and charge duties accurately based on 10-digit HS codes.

If you are already registered with Zonos, no further action is required. Our lodgement platforms and systems will be updated automatically on 17 July 2026 with the new tariff and duty rates and 10-digit HS codes when using the auto-lookup item description.

Information from CBP and postal authorities is subject to change. We continue to encourage customers to

visit our website for updates  about sending outbound parcels to the US from Australia. We also recommend you visit the official websites of the relevant authorities for the most up-to-date information.

Outbound parcels to China

Based on directions from China Customs, parcels outbound from Australia to China must include the receiver's mobile phone number on the Customs Declaration form. China Customs will not accept a recipient landline phone number or email address.

Other international changes

Effective 1 August 2026, the ‘Reason for Export’ categories on CN22 and CN23 labels is changing to align with Universal Postal Union (UPU) requirements. As part of this change:

	- ‘Gift’ will be replaced with ‘Gift (Non?commercial)’
	- ‘Merchandise’ will be replaced with ‘E-commerce goods (B2C)’
	- ‘Commercial sample’ will be replaced with ‘Commercial sale of goods (B2B)’. This should be selected for goods exported as part of a business transaction, whether or not they are sold for money

short_description: I would like to request a full licence for Copilot.
description:
Purpose
This business case seeks approval for a full Microsoft Copilot licence to support my ongoing responsibilities as an Assistant Director working on higher education policy and regulation. In addition to my substantive responsibilities, I regularly perform acting Director duties and provide strategic advice, briefing materials and policy leadership across a range of complex work programs. This requires the ability to rapidly analyse information, develop high-quality written products and provide timely, evidence-based advice to senior ATEC executives including Commissioners and external stakeholders such as TEQSA.
Copilot has become an essential part of my daily workflow that I regularly use to support policy analysis, consultation development, drafting, editing and quality assurance activities. It enables me to work more efficiently, respond more quickly to emerging priorities, and produce high-quality outputs while maintaining appropriate oversight and review processes. Access to a full licence would improve productivity, support the timely provision of advice to senior decision-makers, enhance the quality of outputs and contribute to the effective delivery of significant policy reform work across the higher education sector.
This support is particularly important in the context of the review of the Higher Education Standards Framework (Threshold Standards), a nationally significant piece of work that affects all categories of higher education providers and requires extensive consultation and engagement with stakeholders. Given the breadth, complexity and strategic importance of this work, access to a full Microsoft Copilot licence would provide ongoing value by supporting workforce efficiency, informed decision-making and the delivery of high-quality policy outcomes.

Context
A substantial component of my current work relates to the review of the Higher Education Standards Framework (Threshold Standards). The Threshold Standards are the primary regulatory standards for Australia's higher education sector and have implications across the full range of registered higher education providers, including Australian Universities, University Colleges and non-university higher education providers. Any proposed changes require careful consideration of provider diversity, regulatory burden, governance arrangements, quality assurance expectations, student outcomes and broader public policy objectives. This work requires strategic and holistic analysis to assess system-wide impacts, identify unintended consequences, and ensure that policy proposals remain proportionate, evidence-based and aligned with broader government priorities while supporting a diverse and evolving higher education sector.
This work is undertaken in support of the Higher Education Standards Council (HESC), a newly established ATEC Committee, independent expert body that provides advice on the Threshold Standards to ATEC and engages extensively with the sector through consultation processes. As a result, the work involves preparing discussion papers, analysing evidence, considering stakeholder perspectives, reviewing regulatory frameworks and developing policy options that are capable of application across a complex and diverse sector. It includes benchmarking with other countries to identify best practice solutions.

Current Use of Copilot
I use Copilot every day to support the development and refinement of policy documents. It has proven particularly valuable in reviewing complex drafting, identifying duplication and inconsistencies, strengthening the structure and flow of written material, testing alternative policy approaches and improving the clarity of consultation papers. It also supports the analysis of legislative and regulatory frameworks and assists in translating complex policy issues into language that can be readily understood by stakeholders.
Throughout the development of work associated with the Threshold Standards, I have used Copilot extensively to refine policy arguments, strengthen consultation questions, review draft papers from a stakeholder perspective and ensure policy proposals are communicated clearly and consistently. Given the breadth of issues covered by the Standards, (including governance arrangements, quality assurance, research, cyber security, research security and institutional risk management) the ability to rapidly interrogate and improve draft material has significantly enhanced both efficiency and quality.

Training and Capability
I have undertaken all mandatory departmental training relating to the use of Microsoft Copilot and artificial intelligence tools. In addition, I have completed further learning available through APS Learn, including training provided by the Department of the Treasury to support the responsible and effective use of generative AI within the Australian Public Service.
This additional investment in training has enabled me to develop a strong understanding of the opportunities and limitations of AI-supported work, including privacy, security, information handling and quality assurance requirements. As a result, I am able to use Copilot appropriately, developing complex promotes and integrating what it produces, and using it responsibly while maintaining the necessary human oversight of all work products.

Benefits
The primary benefit of a full Copilot licence is the significant productivity gain it delivers across drafting, editing, analysis and synthesizing complex and large amounts of information, particularly using deep thinking modes. Much of my work involves reviewing lengthy and complex documents, synthesising information from multiple sources and producing material that must be clear, accurate and suitable for engagement with senior executives and external stakeholders. Copilot reduces the administrative burden associated with these tasks and allows more time to be dedicated to policy analysis, stakeholder engagement and strategic thinking.
Copilot also supports workforce efficiency by enabling the rapid development and refinement of advice, briefing materials and policy papers. This allows advice to be provided to managers and senior executives more quickly, while maintaining the quality and rigour expected of policy work. The tool assists in identifying duplication, improving document structure, highlighting inconsistencies and presenting alternative drafting approaches, which accelerates the drafting process without replacing critical judgement or decision-making. Importantly, I review and validate all outputs before being relied upon or provided to decision-makers, ensuring accuracy, relevance and alignment with departmental requirements.
The ability to produce high-quality advice more efficiently is particularly valuable in an environment where policy issues are often complex, time-sensitive and subject to ongoing consultation. For work such as the review of the Higher Education Standards Framework (Threshold Standards), Copilot enables faster turnaround of drafts and briefing materials while supporting thorough analysis and quality assurance. This improves responsiveness to requests from managers and senior executives and contributes to more effective decision-making.
Copilot also contributes to the quality of outputs. It is particularly effective in identifying repetition, improving readability, strengthening policy logic and ensuring documents are written in a way that supports meaningful consultation. Given the national significance of the Threshold Standards and their impact across the higher education sector, high-quality drafting and consultation materials are essential.
The benefits extend beyond individual productivity. Improved efficiency in developing consultation papers, briefing materials, correspondence and policy proposals supports broader ATEC, ministerial and departmental objectives by enabling the timely delivery of reform work while maintaining a high standard of analysis, governance and stakeholder engagement. A full licence would therefore contribute not only to individual capability but also to broader organisational efficiency and the delivery of high-quality policy outcomes.

The Threshold Standards review is a significant piece of work that will influence the regulatory framework applying to Australia's higher education sector. Access to a full Copilot licence will support the efficient delivery of this work, strengthen the quality of policy outputs and consultation materials, and provide ongoing value through increased productivity and capability across my role. This is supported by my demonstrated daily use of Copilot, completion of both mandatory and advanced training, and the substantial benefits it provides in supporting complex higher education policy and regulatory work.

Hi DEWR Cyber Team,
SAP has recently released SAP Security Note 3692165 relating to a DLL Hijacking vulnerability in SAProuter running on Microsoft Windows.

Vulnerability Details


  *   SAP Note: 3692165
  *   Issue: DLL Hijacking vulnerability in SAProuter on Microsoft Windows
  *   Affected Component: SAProuter on Microsoft Windows
  *   Severity: High
  *   CVSS Score: 8.4 / 8.8 (High)
  *   Affected Versions: KRNL64NUC 7.22/7.22EXT, KRNL64UC 7.22/7.22EXT/7.53, SAP_ROUTER 7.53/7.54, KERNEL 7.22/7.53/7.54/7.77/7.89/7.93/9.16/9.17/9.18

This vulnerability impacts SAProuter instances running on Windows servers. Within the DEWR environment, we currently have two SAProuter servers (IPRNSAP200SA and IPRNSAP200SB) hosted in the DEWR DMZ that may be affected.

Given the High severity rating and the potential exposure of externally facing SAProuter systems, could the Cyber Team please engage the DEWR Windows Team as a priority to assess and apply the required SAP patches/remediation to these servers as soon as possible?

The SDO team can assist with identifying the installed SAProuter versions and support any testing activities required following the patch implementation.

Rishi Abrol

short_description: Workforce Forecasting Data Request for QSFS Licence Planning
description:
To support planning for the new QSFS licensing model, I was hoping you may be able to provide historical workforce reporting for the past 12–18 months, including:

Monthly onboarding numbers (new starters)
Monthly offboarding numbers (separations)
Total staff by month
Any available reporting that identifies significant onboarding or offboarding spikes during the period

The purpose of this request is to establish a baseline understanding of workforce movements and staffing trends so we can develop a licence forecasting model. This will help us:

Estimate future licence requirements based on historical onboarding and offboarding patterns.
Maintain an appropriate pool of available licences for new starters.
Avoid over-purchasing licences where staff numbers are declining or remain stable.
Identify periods where licence demand is likely to increase and plan procurement activities in advance.
Reduce the risk of onboarding delays caused by insufficient licence availability.

Hopefully this is fairly straightforward report CIMS can generate -however  if this request is better directed somewhere else please let me know.

short_description: For advice – ACER inquiry on LANTITE data retention (post INC0513532)
description:
OFFICIAL: Sensitive

Good afternoon

Thank you for the advice previously provided by your team regarding Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education (LANTITE) data retention (reference INC0513532). ACER has since advised candidates that their data will be retained for a minimum of 10 years.

ACER has recently raised a number of additional queries. We would appreciate your advice again, on the matters outlined below.

Candidate request
ACER recently received another deletion request from a candidate who registered for the test for first time but has changed their mind, requested a refund, and has asked for their account to be completely deleted. In this case, as the candidate has not sat the LANTITE at all and deletion of their account will not count towards/have any impact on results and technical data reporting, could you please advise if it’s ok for ACER to delete their account which contains their personal data?

Questions from ACER’s data and legal teams
1. This year is the 10th year of LANTITE candidates who sat and met the test standard in 2016 (i.e. their last action). Based on the Higher Education function, Class 20620, disposal action of “Destroy 10 years after last action...”, please advise what the Department would like ACER to do about the data of these candidates.
2. All LANTITE records, including candidates’ personal information collected to process LANTITE results and their results, would constitute Commonwealth records and as a contractor of the Department, ACER will be subject to retaining and disposing the data in accordance with the Higher Education function, Class 20620. Is our understanding correct?
3. Will any of the LANTITE records fall under class 20616?
Regarding Question 3, my preliminary view is that LANTITE records would not fall within Class 20616, as the scale and significance of the test are unlikely to meet the threshold contemplated by that class. By way of context, between 2016 and 2025, a total of 205,558 individuals attempted one or both components of the test. The assessment is a requirement only for students enrolled in accredited initial teacher education courses offered by higher education providers.

Thank you again for your assistance. Please let me know if any further information would be helpful.

short_description: Investigation Required – Dynamics 365 to SharePoint Integration Failure (Unable to Acquire OBO Token
description:
Hey Mike and Service desk team,

Hi Mike and DEWR service desk team,

I have investigated the issue preventing file uploads from the ACES Portal into Dynamics 365 cases.

Issue Summary

This issue is happening in the dev, test, preprod and prod environments.

When users create a Case via the ACES Portal https://asqaacesportal.powerappsportals.com and attempt to upload an attachment, the upload fails and the document is not saved to the associated SharePoint site collection https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/ASQA-D365-ACES-PROD

The same document upload process works successfully from the Dynamics 365 Customer Service Hub https://asqaacesprod.crm6.dynamics.com/main.aspx?appid=52652522-2b85-f011-b4cc-6045bde67be7

Current Findings

The SharePoint permissions appear to be configured correctly:


  *   AAD_APP_ASQA_APP_D365_ASQA_ACES_PROD has Edit permissions to the SharePoint site.
  *   Service account “Service_ASQAACESPR” has Full Control permissions to the SharePoint site collection.
  *   Uploads from the Dynamics 365 Customer Service Hub are successful.

However, when validating Document Management Settings within Dynamics 365, the following error is returned: "The request was aborted: The request was canceled. Unable to acquire OBO token"

Preliminary Assessment

The error indicates a failure in the On-Behalf-Of (OBO) authentication flow used by Dynamics 365 to obtain an Entra ID access token for SharePoint.

This suggests the issue is likely related to one of the following:


  1.  Expired or invalid application credentials.
  2.  Missing or revoked API permissions in Microsoft Entra ID.
  3.  Conditional Access or MFA policies preventing token acquisition.
  4.  Service Principal or App Registration configuration issues.
  5.  SharePoint Server-Based Integration authentication configuration.

Because uploads work from Customer Service Hub but fail from the Portal, there may be a difference in how authentication is being performed between the Portal application and the Dynamics 365 web client.

Recommended Actions


  1.  Review Entra ID App Registration
     *   Confirm the application associated with AAD_APP_ASQA_APP_D365_ASQA_ACES_PROD
     *   Portal authentication components has:
     *   Valid client secret or certificate.
     *   Required Microsoft Graph and SharePoint permissions.
     *   Appropriate admin consent granted.
  2.  Review Conditional Access Policies
     *   Check for recent changes impacting:
     *   Dynamics 365
     *   Power Pages / Portal users
     *   SharePoint Online
     *   Service principals
  3.  Review Dynamics 365 SharePoint Integration
     *   Verify the configuration under: Advanced Settings ? Document Management ? Document Management Settings
     *   and investigate why SharePoint validation is failing with the OBO token error.
  4.  Gather Additional Diagnostic Information
     *   Review:
     *   Browser Developer Console (F12)
     *   Power Platform Admin Centre logs
     *   Entra ID Sign-In Logs
     *   Service Principal Sign-In Logs


     *   Specifically look for:
     *   AADSTS errors
     *   Token acquisition failures
     *   401 / 403 responses
     *   OAuth authorization failures

Environment Details:

Environment Name: ASQA-ACES-PROD
Environment ID: 65abdca2-359e-e167-84c9-b57bd8c580c3

Conclusion

At this stage, the issue does not appear to be caused by SharePoint site permissions. The evidence points toward an authentication failure in the Dynamics 365/Power Pages to SharePoint integration, specifically during the Microsoft Entra ID On-Behalf-Of token acquisition process.

I'd specifically ask the infrastructure/Entra ID team to check Entra ID Sign-in Logs for the service account and application registrations around the time of the failed upload. The OBO token error is usually traceable there within a few minutes.
Other than this I am at a loss, any help would be awesome!

Kind regards,

Micah Cavanough
Microsoft Solutions Functional Consultant
Digital Delivery

[Fiddler] The connection to 'wpad.hosts.network' failed.
Error: ConnectionRefused (0x274d).
System.Net.Sockets.SocketException No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it 10.17.107.18:443

To resolve this issue, I may need to change the network configuration of my workstation and change the proxy settings. As I do not have permission to modify or disable the system proxy/network settings on my workstation to continue with the investigation and could you please advise / provide an approved method to change the settings during the capture. This is a temporary change only to capture the traffic issue during TFVC branching and allow Fiddler capture of https://dev.azure.com/DigitalSolutionsDivision/empl/.

Don

short_description: Bug Report: Microsoft Teams Meeting Window Hidden Behind Windows Voice Access Bar
description:
Location: WFH (ACT)
best contact: 	0424220200 , (02) 6240 8672
asset_id: LA333953

Can you action this bug report to Microsoft please?

Bug Report: Microsoft Teams Meeting Window Hidden Behind Windows Voice Access Bar

Product: Microsoft Teams (Desktop Application)
Platform: Windows 11
Severity: Medium (Accessibility / Usability Issue)
Category: Accessibility / Window Management

Summary
When Windows Voice Access is enabled and a Microsoft Teams meeting starts, the Teams meeting window opens underneath the Voice Access bar at the top of the screen. This causes the meeting title bar to be partially or completely hidden, preventing the window from being moved using normal mouse interaction.
This behaviour appears to be unique to Microsoft Teams. Other Microsoft applications and third-party applications correctly respect the screen space occupied by the Voice Access bar.

Environment

  *   Operating System: Windows 11
  *   Accessibility Feature: Voice Access enabled
  *   Application: Microsoft Teams Desktop Client
  *   Window State: Meeting window (during an active Teams meeting)

Steps to Reproduce

  1.  Enable Voice Access in Windows.
  2.  Ensure the Voice Access bar is docked at the top of the screen.
  3.  Join or start a Microsoft Teams meeting.
  4.  Observe the position of the Teams meeting window when it opens.

Expected Result
The Teams meeting window should open below the Voice Access bar, with the title bar fully visible and accessible, allowing the user to move, resize, or interact with the window normally.

Actual Result
The top portion of the Teams meeting window is positioned underneath the Voice Access bar. The meeting title bar is obscured, making it impossible to click and drag the window to reposition it.

Accessibility Impact
This issue affects users who rely on Windows Voice Access and may prevent them from managing the Teams meeting window effectively. As an accessibility feature, Voice Access should be fully compatible with Microsoft Teams.

Additional Information

  *   The issue appears to affect only Microsoft Teams.
  *   Other Microsoft applications and third-party applications tested do not exhibit this behaviour.
  *   Screenshots attached showing the Teams meeting window hidden beneath the Voice Access bar.

Screenshot Notes
The attached screenshot highlights that the meeting title bar ("Team Nova - Standup") is positioned behind the Voice Access bar. The obscured title bar area has been marked in red to demonstrate the issue.
________________________________

Suggested Investigation: Teams may not be correctly accounting for the reserved screen area (work area) used by the Windows Voice Access toolbar when positioning meeting windows. The application should respect the accessibility UI boundary in the same way as other Windows applications.

Frequency: 100% reproducible on the affected device when Voice Access is enabled.

Examples:

Good Afternoon

You are being contacted as the identified coordinators for the upcoming file review activity.  If we have not contacted you via the correct group inbox, please provide this for future communications.

Background
In line with the Senate Continuing Order for Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files<https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Chamber_documents/Senate_chamber_documents/standingorders/d00/Procedural_orders_of_continuing_effect/d05#Procedural-orders_12>, the department is preparing to publish its next list of official file titles created between 1st January 2026 to 30th June 2026. This list will be made available on the following department's websites to support transparency and accountability in public administration.

Senate Continuing Order - Listing of Departmental Files - Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Government<https://www.dewr.gov.au/about-us/corporate-reporting/senate-order-listings/senate-continuing-order-listing-departmental-files>

The Information Management and SharePoint (IM&S) Section is currently compiling the listings, which include official files created in Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint sites.

What to Expect as a coordinator

  *   IM&S will provide each group with a listing of relevant file titles for review no later than 9 July 2026. Your role is to coordinate the review for your group.
  *   Each group will have 11 business days to review their listings.  Due to clearance requirements this will be the maximum amount of time allowed for the review.
  *   Once the review is complete, groups should consolidate and return a single amended list to IM&S.
  *   If further clarification is needed, IM&S will follow up directly with the relevant group to resolve any outstanding redaction or exemption issues.

Review Process
Groups are asked to confirm whether file titles are suitable for inclusion or require redaction. This is broadly based on the following criteria:

  *   Listings may contain acronyms, and groups are asked to ensure these are spelled out in full for clarity.

  *   Titles suitable for inclusion:
     *   Those relating to policy advising functions
     *   Development of legislation
     *   Matters of public administration
  *   Titles that may be suitable for redaction:
     *   Commercially confidential information
     *   Classified information
     *   National security matters
     *   Personal identifying information

More detailed guidance will be provided with the file lists.  If you have any questions about the process or have concerns about meeting the deadline please contact InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au<mailto:InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au>.

Thanks

description:
Hi all,

Thanks
Bethany

From: DEWR - ETD Information Management <InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au>
Sent: Friday, 3 July 2026 1:56 PM
To: DEWR - Deputy Secretary Employment and Workforce <DeputySecretaryEmploymentandWorkforce@dewr.gov.au>
Cc: CARPENTER,Julie <Julie.Carpenter@dewr.gov.au>; CRAIGIE,Justine <Justine.Craigie@dewr.gov.au>
Subject: Upcoming Review July 2026: Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Good Afternoon

You are being contacted as the identified coordinators for the upcoming file review activity.  If we have not contacted you via the correct group inbox, please provide this for future communications.

Background
In line with the Senate Continuing Order for Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files<https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Chamber_documents/Senate_chamber_documents/standingorders/d00/Procedural_orders_of_continuing_effect/d05#Procedural-orders_12>, the department is preparing to publish its next list of official file titles created between 1st January 2026 to 30th June 2026. This list will be made available on the following department's websites to support transparency and accountability in public administration.

Senate Continuing Order - Listing of Departmental Files - Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Government<https://www.dewr.gov.au/about-us/corporate-reporting/senate-order-listings/senate-continuing-order-listing-departmental-files>

The Information Management and SharePoint (IM&S) Section is currently compiling the listings, which include official files created in Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint sites.

What to Expect as a coordinator

  *   IM&S will provide each group with a listing of relevant file titles for review no later than 9 July 2026. Your role is to coordinate the review for your group.

Logged in later that day ~10.30am after secure boot work finished and fail back to primaries had been completed by Atul, services started without issue.

My executive, Erin, is looking to establish a communication forum for her branch that encourages positive engagement, effective communication, and connection across the team. We have previously had a team's branch group chat however, we would like to explore whether there is an option to moderate communications-for example, allowing Erin, the directors, and/or myself to approve posts/messages before they are shared, while still enabling staff to interact and engage with content.

My understanding is that a Teams channel may offer some of these controls, but I'm also aware that channel posts can sometimes receive less visibility than group chat messages if notifications aren't enabled.

You are being contacted as the identified coordinators for the upcoming file review activity.  If we have not contacted you via the correct group inbox, please provide this for future communications.

Background
In line with the Senate Continuing Order for Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files<https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Chamber_documents/Senate_chamber_documents/standingorders/d00/Procedural_orders_of_continuing_effect/d05#Procedural-orders_12>, the department is preparing to publish its next list of official file titles created between 1st January 2026 to 30th June 2026. This list will be made available on the following department’s websites to support transparency and accountability in public administration.

Senate Continuing Order — Listing of Departmental Files - Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Government<https://www.dewr.gov.au/about-us/corporate-reporting/senate-order-listings/senate-continuing-order-listing-departmental-files>

The Information Management and SharePoint (IM&S) Section is currently compiling the listings, which include official files created in Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint sites.

What to Expect as a coordinator

  *   IM&S will provide each group with a listing of relevant file titles for review no later than 9 July 2026. Your role is to coordinate the review for your group.
  *   Each group will have 11 business days to review their listings.  Due to clearance requirements this will be the maximum amount of time allowed for the review.
  *   Once the review is complete, groups should consolidate and return a single amended list to IM&S.
  *   If further clarification is needed, IM&S will follow up directly with the relevant group to resolve any outstanding redaction or exemption issues.

  *   Titles suitable for inclusion:
     *   Those relating to policy advising functions
     *   Development of legislation
     *   Matters of public administration
  *   Titles that may be suitable for redaction:
     *   Commercially confidential information
     *   Classified information
     *   National security matters
     *   Personal identifying information
