Hi Dilani

Thanks for send through your feedback on the course.  Based on this we have incorporated the following changes to the content.  Please let us know if you have any concerns with this approach.

The module does not currently provide any details of the legal framework for record retention, which we suggest is useful to ensure that staff have a good understanding of their legal obligations, such as:
N/A
What is a Commonwealth record subject to retention obligations under the Archives Act 1983 (Archives Act)
Incorporated into the section 2 Why Information Matters, Information Assets and the Archives Act 1993.

When you create, receive, or use information as part of your work, it may be considered an information asset and therefore a Commonwealth record.
Information assets provide evidence of government business, including decisions, actions, approvals, advice, and transactions. They are also subject to retention and disposal requirements under the Archives Act 1983.
The offence for destruction, disposal, transfer, damage or alteration of Commonwealth records in section 24(1) of the Archives Act
Incorporated into the section 2  Why Information Matters, Information Assets and the Archives Act 1993.

Under section 24(1) of the Act, it is an offence to destroy a Commonwealth record unless the destruction is authorised and carried out in accordance with an approved information management process. Unauthorised disposal of records may result in penalties being applied under the Act.
When such conduct is authorised under section 24(2) of the Archives Act.
Not necessary for our awareness course as staff do not need to know the legislative detail of how authorisation occurs under section 24(2).  In accordance with the IM Policy, all disposal of Information Assets/Commonwealth Records (excluding ROT information) is conducted by the IM&S team.

Staff need to be aware that they must not destroy an information asset unless under an approved information management process which includes the relevant authorisation.

Details of section 24(2)(c) will be added to the ROT section to recognise the use of NAP.
The module refers to discarding of 'Redundant, Obsolete, and Trivial' information. We suggest making it clearer the link to section 24(2)(c) of the Archives Act, which authorises disposal of Commonwealth records in accordance with normal administrative practice.
Incorporated into section 4 What you need to know - ...Discard what you don't need

While this information may have been useful when created, it is no longer needed for the departments work and should not be kept.  Section 24(2)(c) of the Archives Act 1983 allows for the disposal of ROT information as part of Normal Administrative Practice.
In relation to the sections on access and use, we suggest the module make clear that the Privacy Act 1988 and secrecy provisions may impose additional restrictions on who is authorised to access or use information than what is required from an information management perspective.
Incorporated into section 2 Why Information Matters under the section of the definitions for the stages of the Information Lifecycle under Access.

Always ensure you are authorised to access, use and share information. Privacy, security and legislative requirements may impose additional restrictions beyond information management requirements.
In relation to the section on destroy, it does not appear to be completely consistent with the ability of staff to dispose of records in accordance with normal administrative practice.
Incorporated into Destroy section

Disposal of information assets is managed corporately. You support this by saving information in approved systems so it can be disposed of at the appropriate time. As part of your daily activities, you should also assess if any of your information is Redundant, Obsolete or Trivial (ROT). There is no requirement to save ROT information into an approved system. You are allowed to securely dispose of ROT information when no longer useful.
In relation to the section on 'Protect information when required', we suggest making clear that this aligns with the department's obligation under Australian Privacy Principle 11.1 to take reasonable steps to protect personal information from 'misuse, interference and loss; and from unauthorised access, modification or disclosure.
Incorporated into section 4 What you need to know under the section of Protect Information when required,

Protecting information is not only an information management requirement. The Australian Privacy Principle 11.1 requires that additional controls are applied to protect personal information from loss, misuse and unauthorised access or disclosure.
In relation to the section on 'Include the important details' you may want to make clear that these actions can assist the department in being able to efficiently undertake searches for documents subject to FOI or privacy requests.
Incorporated into section 4 What you need to know under the section of Include the important details

When you include these details it helps support the department in efficiently responding to requests for information, including Freedom of Information (FOI) and privacy requests.
We suggest including details of the privacy and security risks in retaining records for longer than is necessary, and encouraging the destruction of records as soon as it is authorised under the Archives Act. It could also be noted that there is another benefit in that once they have been destroyed, records can no longer be subject to an FOI request.
Incorporated into section 2 Why Information Matters under the section of the definitions for the stages of the Information Lifecycle under Destroy. Just a brief paragraph about how information should not be retained for longer than necessary.

Retaining information longer than necessary can increase privacy, security and storage risks. Once information assets have met the retention requirements in accordance with the Archives Act 1983, and are no longer needed for business, disposal can commence.
You may want to add a question to the knowledge check scenarios related to the legal obligations.
Not necessary for our knowledge check scenario questions, as our course is to influence behaviour regarding saving and managing information not to test detailed legislative knowledge.

Archives Act obligations have been added to the course.  Privacy obligations are covered in separate training.

Thanks, and have a great day.

Subject: Upcoming Review July 2026: Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Good Afternoon

You are being contacted as the identified coordinators for the upcoming file review activity.  If we have not contacted you via the correct group inbox, please provide this for future communications.

Background
In line with the Senate Continuing Order for Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files<https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Chamber_documents/Senate_chamber_documents/standingorders/d00/Procedural_orders_of_continuing_effect/d05#Procedural-orders_12>, the department is preparing to publish its next list of official file titles created between 1st January 2026 to 30th June 2026. This list will be made available on the following department's websites to support transparency and accountability in public administration.

Senate Continuing Order - Listing of Departmental Files - Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Government<https://www.dewr.gov.au/about-us/corporate-reporting/senate-order-listings/senate-continuing-order-listing-departmental-files>

The Information Management and SharePoint (IM&S) Section is currently compiling the listings, which include official files created in Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint sites.

What to Expect as a coordinator

  *   IM&S will provide each group with a listing of relevant file titles for review no later than 9 July 2026. Your role is to coordinate the review for your group.
  *   Each group will have 11 business days to review their listings.  Due to clearance requirements this will be the maximum amount of time allowed for the review.
  *   Once the review is complete, groups should consolidate and return a single amended list to IM&S.
  *   If further clarification is needed, IM&S will follow up directly with the relevant group to resolve any outstanding redaction or exemption issues.

Review Process
Groups are asked to confirm whether file titles are suitable for inclusion or require redaction. This is broadly based on the following criteria:

  *   Listings may contain acronyms, and groups are asked to ensure these are spelled out in full for clarity.

  *   Titles suitable for inclusion:
     *   Those relating to policy advising functions
     *   Development of legislation
     *   Matters of public administration
  *   Titles that may be suitable for redaction:
     *   Commercially confidential information
     *   Classified information
     *   National security matters
     *   Personal identifying information

More detailed guidance will be provided with the file lists.  If you have any questions about the process or have concerns about meeting the deadline please contact InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au<mailto:InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au>.

Thanks

short_description: Request for Home Printing – Commissioner Fiona Nash
description:
Good morning,

The Hon Fiona Nash, Australian Tertiary Education Commission (ATEC) Commissioner and Regional Education Commissioner (REC), is seeking approval for home printing arrangements.

As Commissioner Nash works entirely remotely, access to home printing is necessary to support her day-to-day operations. She regularly requires hard copies of ATEC and REC briefing materials, meeting papers, presentations, and stakeholder engagement documents. These documents are often used during meetings, events, and speaking engagements where printed materials are required for reference, review, and annotation.

Given the Commissioner’s fully remote working arrangements and the time-sensitive nature of many documents, office-based printing is not a practical alternative.

Commissioner Nash is requesting the following equipment:

  *   A colour printer with duplex printing and scan-to-email functionality.
  *   A small Class B safe for the secure storage of printed materials (only if required).
  *   A small Class B shredder for appropriate destruction of documents (only if required).

Please find attached an email from David Turvey providing provisional approval for this request. However, he has requested that costings be provided before final approval is given.

Good Afternoon

You are being contacted as the identified coordinators for the upcoming file review activity.  If we have not contacted you via the correct group inbox, please provide this for future communications.

Background
In line with the Senate Continuing Order for Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files<https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Chamber_documents/Senate_chamber_documents/standingorders/d00/Procedural_orders_of_continuing_effect/d05#Procedural-orders_12>, the department is preparing to publish its next list of official file titles created between 1st January 2026 to 30th June 2026. This list will be made available on the following department's websites to support transparency and accountability in public administration.

Senate Continuing Order - Listing of Departmental Files - Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Government<https://www.dewr.gov.au/about-us/corporate-reporting/senate-order-listings/senate-continuing-order-listing-departmental-files>

The Information Management and SharePoint (IM&S) Section is currently compiling the listings, which include official files created in Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint sites.

What to Expect as a coordinator

  *   IM&S will provide each group with a listing of relevant file titles for review no later than 9 July 2026. Your role is to coordinate the review for your group.
  *   Each group will have 11 business days to review their listings.  Due to clearance requirements this will be the maximum amount of time allowed for the review.
  *   Once the review is complete, groups should consolidate and return a single amended list to IM&S.
  *   If further clarification is needed, IM&S will follow up directly with the relevant group to resolve any outstanding redaction or exemption issues.

Review Process
Groups are asked to confirm whether file titles are suitable for inclusion or require redaction. This is broadly based on the following criteria:

  *   Listings may contain acronyms, and groups are asked to ensure these are spelled out in full for clarity.

  *   Titles suitable for inclusion:
     *   Those relating to policy advising functions
     *   Development of legislation
     *   Matters of public administration
  *   Titles that may be suitable for redaction:
     *   Commercially confidential information
     *   Classified information
     *   National security matters
     *   Personal identifying information

More detailed guidance will be provided with the file lists.  If you have any questions about the process or have concerns about meeting the deadline please contact InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au<mailto:InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au>.

Thanks

description:

Amber Horne

To: TARRANT,Mandy <Mandy.Tarrant@dewr.gov.au>; CARPENTER,Julie <Julie.Carpenter@dewr.gov.au>; CAMERON-TAYLOR,Phoebe <Phoebe.Cameron-Taylor@dewr.gov.au>

Subject: Connected Beginnings File Management Plan

Good morning, Mandy, Julie, and Phoebe,
Thank you for meeting with me a few weeks ago to discuss an approach to file management in the Connected Beginnings team. I appreciated the opportunity to discuss our current approach and explore improvements.
Our team manages both procurements (e.g. for contractors to work in the team, for businesses who deliver specific services) and grant management (e.g. progress and financial reporting, milestone payments, Deeds of Variation) and we want to ensure we are following the correct file management processes for both streams of work.
As we move forward with developing a file management plan for the Connected Beginnings team, I'm seeking clarification on the below:

  *   Could you please confirm whether our program management documents (e.g. grant agreements, progress and financial reporting, delegate decisions etc.) are not required to be saved in TRIM (Content Manager) and can instead be stored in SharePoint?
     *   We understand other teams in the branch were advised to save their final copies of program related documents in TRIM, and we would like to ensure there is a consistent approach across the branch.
     *   Are there any risks with using SharePoint for final documents when a MoG occurs?
  *   Could you please clarify what procurement documents must be stored in TRIM (Content Manager)? For example, does this include all associated correspondence?
  *   Is there a recommended approach to link our SharePoint site with TRIM to enable more streamlined saving and recordkeeping processes?
  *   When will I:Drive become obsolete?
     *   When I:Drive does become obsolete, would it be possible to obtain approval to continue saving and accessing/editing a single Excel spreadsheet?
Thank you in advance for your support.
Kind regards,
Amber

Subject: Upcoming Review July 2026: Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Good Afternoon

You are being contacted as the identified coordinators for the upcoming file review activity.  If we have not contacted you via the correct group inbox, please provide this for future communications.

Background
In line with the Senate Continuing Order for Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files<https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Chamber_documents/Senate_chamber_documents/standingorders/d00/Procedural_orders_of_continuing_effect/d05#Procedural-orders_12>, the department is preparing to publish its next list of official file titles created between 1st January 2026 to 30th June 2026. This list will be made available on the following department's websites to support transparency and accountability in public administration.

Senate Continuing Order - Listing of Departmental Files - Department of Education, Australian Government<https://www.education.gov.au/about-department/corporate-reporting/senate-order-listings/senate-continuing-order-listing-departmental-files>

The Information Management and SharePoint (IM&S) Section is currently compiling the listings, which include official files created in Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint sites.

What to Expect as a coordinator

  *   IM&S will provide each group with a listing of relevant file titles for review no later than 9 July 2026. Your role is to coordinate the review for your group.
  *   Each group will have 11 business days to review their listings.  Due to clearance requirements this will be the maximum amount of time allowed for the review.
  *   Once the review is complete, groups should consolidate and return a single amended list to IM&S.
  *   If further clarification is needed, IM&S will follow up directly with the relevant group to resolve any outstanding redaction or exemption issues.

Review Process
Groups are asked to confirm whether file titles are suitable for inclusion or require redaction. This is broadly based on the following criteria:

  *   Listings may contain acronyms, and groups are asked to ensure these are spelled out in full for clarity.

  *   Titles suitable for inclusion:
     *   Those relating to policy advising functions
     *   Development of legislation
     *   Matters of public administration
  *   Titles that may be suitable for redaction:
     *   Commercially confidential information
     *   Classified information
     *   National security matters
     *   Personal identifying information

More detailed guidance will be provided with the file lists.  If you have any questions about the process or have concerns about meeting the deadline please contact InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au<mailto:InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au>.

Thanks

Subject: Upcoming Review July 2026: Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files

Good Afternoon

You are being contacted as the identified coordinators for the upcoming file review activity.  If we have not contacted you via the correct group inbox, please provide this for future communications.

Background
In line with the Senate Continuing Order for Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files<https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Chamber_documents/Senate_chamber_documents/standingorders/d00/Procedural_orders_of_continuing_effect/d05#Procedural-orders_12>, the department is preparing to publish its next list of official file titles created between 1st January 2026 to 30th June 2026. This list will be made available on the following department's websites to support transparency and accountability in public administration.

Senate Continuing Order - Listing of Departmental Files - Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Government<https://www.dewr.gov.au/about-us/corporate-reporting/senate-order-listings/senate-continuing-order-listing-departmental-files>

The Information Management and SharePoint (IM&S) Section is currently compiling the listings, which include official files created in Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint sites.

What to Expect as a coordinator

  *   IM&S will provide each group with a listing of relevant file titles for review no later than 9 July 2026. Your role is to coordinate the review for your group.
  *   Each group will have 11 business days to review their listings.  Due to clearance requirements this will be the maximum amount of time allowed for the review.
  *   Once the review is complete, groups should consolidate and return a single amended list to IM&S.
  *   If further clarification is needed, IM&S will follow up directly with the relevant group to resolve any outstanding redaction or exemption issues.

Review Process
Groups are asked to confirm whether file titles are suitable for inclusion or require redaction. This is broadly based on the following criteria:

  *   Listings may contain acronyms, and groups are asked to ensure these are spelled out in full for clarity.

  *   Titles suitable for inclusion:
     *   Those relating to policy advising functions
     *   Development of legislation
     *   Matters of public administration
  *   Titles that may be suitable for redaction:
     *   Commercially confidential information
     *   Classified information
     *   National security matters
     *   Personal identifying information

More detailed guidance will be provided with the file lists.  If you have any questions about the process or have concerns about meeting the deadline please contact InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au<mailto:InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au>.

Thanks

     *   Matters of public administration
  *   Titles that may be suitable for redaction:

     *   National security matters
     *   Personal identifying information

More detailed guidance will be provided with the file lists.  If you have any questions about the process or have concerns about meeting the deadline please contact InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au<mailto:InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au>.

Thanks

Subject: Upcoming Review July 2026: Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Good Afternoon

You are being contacted as the identified coordinators for the upcoming file review activity.  If we have not contacted you via the correct group inbox, please provide this for future communications.

Background
In line with the Senate Continuing Order for Indexed Lists of Departmental and Agency Files<https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Chamber_documents/Senate_chamber_documents/standingorders/d00/Procedural_orders_of_continuing_effect/d05#Procedural-orders_12>, the department is preparing to publish its next list of official file titles created between 1st January 2026 to 30th June 2026. This list will be made available on the following department’s websites to support transparency and accountability in public administration.

Senate Continuing Order — Listing of Departmental Files - Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Government<https://www.dewr.gov.au/about-us/corporate-reporting/senate-order-listings/senate-continuing-order-listing-departmental-files>

The Information Management and SharePoint (IM&S) Section is currently compiling the listings, which include official files created in Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint sites.

What to Expect as a coordinator

  *   IM&S will provide each group with a listing of relevant file titles for review no later than 9 July 2026. Your role is to coordinate the review for your group.
  *   Each group will have 11 business days to review their listings.  Due to clearance requirements this will be the maximum amount of time allowed for the review.
  *   Once the review is complete, groups should consolidate and return a single amended list to IM&S.
  *   If further clarification is needed, IM&S will follow up directly with the relevant group to resolve any outstanding redaction or exemption issues.

Review Process
Groups are asked to confirm whether file titles are suitable for inclusion or require redaction. This is broadly based on the following criteria:

  *   Listings may contain acronyms, and groups are asked to ensure these are spelled out in full for clarity.

  *   Titles suitable for inclusion:
     *   Those relating to policy advising functions
     *   Development of legislation
     *   Matters of public administration
  *   Titles that may be suitable for redaction:
     *   Commercially confidential information
     *   Classified information
     *   National security matters
     *   Personal identifying information

More detailed guidance will be provided with the file lists.  If you have any questions about the process or have concerns about meeting the deadline please contact InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au<mailto:InformationManagementInbox@dewr.gov.au>.

Thanks

We are contacting you as our team consulted you regarding the Information Management Policy, approved September 2025, and would like to seek your views on the following

  *   Alignment with your current practices, systems and policies in particular appropriate use of responsible AI usage and systems within the M365 environment

  *   Relevance and usefulness of knowledge check examples and scenarios

What's changing?
The new course has been designed to reflect current policies, practices and expectations, and to provide a more engaging and practical learning experience for staff. The content has interactive elements and aligns with the updated Information Management Policy (approved September 2025).

The Information Management Awareness course aims to:

  *   Provides a streamlined learning experience, approximately 30 minutes including knowledge check questions).
  *   Strengthen staff understanding of their responsibilities in managing information.
  *   Promote good practice in creating, storing, securing and disposing of information. Support compliance with legislative and policy requirements.

short_description: FW: CyberArk / Ansible Automation Platform integration
description:
From: RENNER,Miika <Miika.Renner@dewr.gov.au>
Sent: Wednesday, 1 July 2026 5:36 PM
To: DEWR - TSD Cyber Security Services <ITSecurity@dewr.gov.au>
Cc: COLE,Abbey <Abbey.Cole@dewr.gov.au>; DEWR - Linux Team <LinuxTeam@dewr.gov.au>; TAPLIN,Joel <Joel.TAPLIN@dewr.gov.au>; PUROSKI,Saso <Saso.Puroski@dewr.gov.au>
Subject: CyberArk / Ansible Automation Platform integration [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi,

The Linux team would like to use the Ansible Automation Platform along with Event Driven Ansible to automate the rotation and retrieval of secrets in Linux environments.

A challenge we is the large number of service accounts which require password rotations which cannot be automated through CyberArk alone.

These accounts are used for things like:

* Active Directory ‘domain join’ accounts used to join a newly built Linux host to a domain using Ansible Automation Platform (AAP)
* Service accounts for email alerts used for AAP and OpenShift Container Platform
* Accounts for authenticating through the proxy in Ansible Automation tasks such as retrieving updated software
* Accounts for VMWare VRA automated host builds through Ansible Automation Platform

As Ansible Automation Platform does not currently have access to CyberArk, it must retrieve account credentials from ansible ‘vault’ files.  These are encrypted files where secrets are stored and referred to as variables in playbooks. These variables can be retrieved by AAP after decryption using a ‘vault’ credential during playbook runs.  Updating service account credentials means logging into CyberArk, rotating the credential, copying it and pasting it into the right vault file for the right variable that needs updating.

We as a team have now got a fairly large number of service accounts and a lot of ansible code, and trying to remember which vault file and variable corresponds to which service account can be a challenge.  We’ve done our best to use descriptive service account names but there’s only so many characters in an account name to work with…  We have an internal wiki page mapping most service accounts to the relevant vault file but it’s updated on a best-effort basis.  When we write ansible to automate tasks we don’t always remember to document what’s what, and after a year the memory is pretty iffy.

Thankfully CyberArk have created an Ansible Automation Collection which is included in AAP as part of AAP’s ‘Red Hat Certified’ software.  The Linux team could leverage this collection to make CyberArk credential rotation and password retrieval easier and less error prone.  We could also leverage Event Driven Ansible to automatically rotate credentials as they expire.

Some links / relevant information

Red Hat blog post on CyberArk / AAP integration along with examples: Automating Security with CyberArk and Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform<https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/automating-security-with-cyberark-and-red-hat-ansible-automation-platform>
CyberArk Collection on Github: GitHub - cyberark/ansible-security-automation-collection: CyberArk Ansible Security Automation Collection · GitHub<https://github.com/cyberark/ansible-security-automation-collection>
Example playbook showing how to log in to CyberArk, retrieve a credential and log off: ansible-security-automation-collection/docs/cyberark_account.md at master · cyberark/ansible-security-automation-collection · GitHub<https://github.com/cyberark/ansible-security-automation-collection/blob/master/docs/cyberark_account.md>
Examples of integrating CyberArk with Event Driven Ansible as an event source: ansible-security-automation-collection/docs/cyberark_eda.md at master · cyberark/ansible-security-automation-collection · GitHub<https://github.com/cyberark/ansible-security-automation-collection/blob/master/docs/cyberark_eda.md>
Youtube video demonstrating how to retrieve CyberArk secrets dynamically and use them within AAP playbooks: Dynamic Secrets in Ansible Automation Platform with CyberArk's Central Credential Provider<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VWmoTdSgoWg>
The playbook being used in the above demo: yt-ansible-dynamic-secrets/roles/ccp-dynamic-secrets/tasks/main.yml at main · infamousjoeg/yt-ansible-dynamic-secrets · GitHub<https://github.com/infamousjoeg/yt-ansible-dynamic-secrets/blob/main/roles/ccp-dynamic-secrets/tasks/main.yml>

Note that if I understand the ‘Dynamic Secrets’ vid correctly, we can use that workflow to retrieve secrets and use them in AAP without requiring the purchase and setup of CyberArk Conjur, saving the Dept a ton of time/money!  It’s more clunky but it’ll do the job.

Thank you for considering this proposal. ?

Regards,

Miika Renner
Linux System Administrator

short_description: Advice on Dual IT Access for Treasury Secondee
description:
Hi Team,

I am seeking advice regarding a proposed secondment arrangement involving a Treasury employee, who will be joining DEWR in a hybrid role.
The current proposal is for the employee to work three days per week with DEWR and two days per week with Treasury as part of a Taskforce arrangement. Discussions between the respective SES Band 1 officers are still underway, and a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) is being developed.

Before progressing the arrangement, could you please advise whether it is feasible for the employee to be provided with dual IT system access across both agencies for the duration of the secondment?
In particular, we would appreciate any advice on:


  *   Whether DEWR can provide ICT access while the employee maintains Treasury access.

short_description: Request to Enable Anonymous/Public Access for HCIS QA Power Pages Site for UAT
description:
Hi Service Desk,

Could you please route this request to the appropriate Power Platform / Digital Collaboration team for action.

We are currently preparing for UAT of the HCIS solution and have identified an issue with the QA Power Pages site:
https://swa-hcis-qa2.powerappsportals.com<https://swa-hcis-qa2.powerappsportals.com/>

The site appears to be configured as a private/authenticated website. Users are intermittently receiving messages indicating that tenant administrator approval is required to access the site, despite being granted access and added to the relevant permissions.
This is causing issues with QA validation and user testing.

The intended production configuration for HCIS is an anonymous/public-facing Power Pages website, therefore we would like the QA environment to mirror the planned production access model for UAT purposes.

Request
Please review the configuration of the HCIS QA Power Pages site and:

  1.  Enable anonymous/public access to the website.
  2.  Remove any requirement for Microsoft 365 authentication or tenant admin consent to access the site.
  3.  Confirm the site's visibility settings align with the intended production configuration for HCIS.
  4.  Advise if any additional actions are required from the SWA team.

Business Impact
The current configuration is preventing reliable UAT access and introducing unnecessary testing blockers. The HCIS project is progressing towards go-live later this month, and the QA environment needs to be available for testing without authentication issues.
Please treat this request as a priority as it impacts upcoming UAT and readiness activities.

Kind regards,

Vinod Bhupathy he/him

short_description: FW: Information Management Awareness Course - Consultation Draft
description:
Good afternoon,

Thank you for the opportunity to review the updated Information Management learning materials.

I've made some suggested changes in track based on recent updates to our Information Management Policy (which is due to be released to the department in the next week or two).
My updates are mainly focused on AI, to ensure the material aligns closely with the updated Government guidance (including Artificial Intelligence (AI) Plan for the APS<https://www.digital.gov.au/policy/ai/australian-public-service-ai-plan-2025> and the National Archives of Australia guidance on information management for records created using AI technologies<https://www.naa.gov.au/information-management/manage-information-assets/types-information/information-management-records-created-using-artificial-intelligence-ai-technologies>).

The changes strengthen messaging around verifying AI-generated content, understanding when AI outputs may need to be retained and reinforcing that AI-generated information is subject to the same recordkeeping obligations as other information assets.

I've also made a few minor updates to improve clarity around capturing sufficient context for decisions, the use of metadata and added a caveat to the ROT guidance. I note the ROT factsheet<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/DESE-InformationManagement/Shared%20Documents/Forms/QRGs.aspx?id=%2Fsites%2FDESE%2DInformationManagement%2FShared%20Documents%2FIdentifying%20and%20Discarding%20ROT%20Information%2Epdf&parent=%2Fsites%2FDESE%2DInformationManagement%2FShared%20Documents> may also need to be updated to reflect the same messaging.

Thanks again for including to us and we look forward to seeing the final product.

Thanks
Claudia

Good afternoon DEWR Service Desk and Enterprise Management team,

I am emailing to implement a fix for a problem we are having with our Objective software.
The vendor recommends the following as a fix for the issue, I have converted the command into powershell, can this be run with admin permissions? And can it be deployed to testing asqa staff first then to all asqa staff?
The command is as follows:
Start-Process -FilePath C:\WINDOWS\System32\fsutil.exe -ArgumentList "8dot3name set 0" -NoNewWindow -Wait
Start-Process -FilePath C:\WINDOWS\System32\fsutil.exe -ArgumentList "8dot3name set C: 0" -NoNewWindow -Wait

Or alternatively you can configure it as a group policy, probably easier and more persistent.
Any advice or improvements on this would be highly appreciated.

short_description: Request to Disable npintaksauc1laat AKS Cluster Auto-Upgrade and Node OS Upgrade
description:
Hi Service Desk, Azure Services,

Can you help with updating the configuration of our AKS cluster npintaksauc1laat in resource group NP-INT-AUC1-LAAT?

We have identified that automatic cluster maintenance operations (node OS upgrades and potentially control plane auto-upgrades) are occurring during business hours and preventing any cluster changes. This is leading to temporary locks on the cluster and preventing manual scaling operations during that time.

Reason for script execution

  *   Automatic node OS upgrade operations are triggering daily "update in progress" states
  *   These operations block node pool scaling and impact workload availability during peak hours
  *   We intend to manage upgrades manually during controlled maintenance windows

Expected outcome

  *   Disable automatic node OS upgrades
  *   Disable automatic Kubernetes version upgrades
  *   Restore full control over cluster scaling and maintenance scheduling

To prevent further disruption, could you please execute the following Azure CLI commands to disable automatic upgrades?

$aksServiceName = 'npintaksauc1laat'
$aksRG = 'NP-INT-AUC1-LAAT'

az aks update --resource-group $aksRG --name $aksServiceName --node-os-upgrade-channel None

az aks update --resource-group $aksRG --name $aksServiceName --auto-upgrade-channel none

Please let me know if you need any additional details.

Kind regards,
Josip Turcic
Automation Engineer

short_description: O:\ Drive Write Access Exemption Request
description:
Good morning,

I'm writing to request an exemption to retain write access to the O:\Data Dev Store, which is scheduled to be converted to read-only in the near future.

Our team administers a critical database that relies on an SSIS package hosted on this drive. The solution includes a number of configuration files, connection files, and package-related assets that must be both read from and written to during normal operation and maintenance. Converting the drive to read-only would prevent updates to these components and is likely to disrupt the functionality and reliability of the service.

SSIS packages can't reliably read/write directly to SharePoint paths as packages require a file system-based location for reliable read/write operations. SharePoint does not provide the necessary file system access or transactional consistency needed for package execution, making it unsuitable as a replacement.

Specifically, we require write access for:

  *   Updating SSIS package configurations
  *   Maintaining connection strings and environment-specific settings
  *   Deploying and modifying package files as part of ongoing support and enhancements

Without this access, we would face operational risks, including failed jobs, inability to apply urgent fixes, and potential data processing interruptions.

The O:\Data Dev Store has limited access for a controlled group of 4 users.

Please let me know if you need further details or would like to discuss this request.

Thanks for your consideration.

Kind regards,
Kara Pohl
Assistant Director
Data Development and Strategy | Data and Insights
Quality, Strategy and Improvement

short_description: Advice Required – Feasibility of Mutual TLS for FNMS Inventory Uploads
description:
Hi Team,

We are seeking Cyber Security Services' advice on the feasibility of implementing Mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication across all devices (clients and servers) for FlexNet Manager Suite (FNMS) inventory uploads.

The last advice I received was that Intune-supplied certificates are still in a Proof of Concept stage—can you please confirm if this is still the case? If so, we can disregard the detailed assessment below as it would likely prevent full mTLS adoption.

Background / Why This Is Being Assessed
--------------------------------------------------
We are currently enabling Cloud PC inventory uploads into FNMS. As part of this, SoftwareOne have successfully tested Mutual TLS authentication using existing “Machine Shed” (internally issued) certificates.
Mutual TLS is required for Cloud PCs because:
- They are Azure Entra–joined only (WORKGROUP)
- They do not have an on-prem Active Directory computer account, unlike domain-joined SOE devices
As such, standard Windows authentication cannot be used

Additionally, FNMS Inventory Beacons can only support a single authentication method at a time (either mTLS or Windows/Basic authentication).

Because of this limitation, we are assessing whether it is feasible to transition all FNMS inventory uploads to Mutual TLS, rather than introducing a separate beacon for Cloud PCs.

What We Need Advice On
-------------------------------
We are requesting advice on whether it is feasible to standardise on Mutual TLS across all FNMS-integrated devices.
Specifically:
1. Certificate Coverage
      •	Are client authentication certificates already issued to: 
               o	ENETAPP servers (initial checks indicate this is likely the case)?
               o	End-user devices across the environment?
2. Certificate Deployment Capability
      •	Can certificates be reliably deployed to all endpoints (e.g. via GPO, Intune)?
      •	Are there any known gaps, exclusions, or device types where this would not be possible?
3. Security & Policy Considerations
      •	Are there any security policies or design constraints that would prevent enforcing Mutual TLS across all devices?
      •	Any risks or concerns with mandating certificate-based authentication for this use case?

If full Mutual TLS adoption is not feasible, we will proceed with deploying a dedicated FNMS Inventory Beacon for Cloud PCs using Mutual TLS, while retaining existing authentication for other devices.

Cheers,
Elvis

description:

Our new Production Windows 2022 servers for Corporate Directory are ready to run the CD batch jobs. This will need to be implemented in a gradual manner to ensure there is as little impact as possible.

Batch Jobs:
- PA_CD_AccessRoles
- PA_CD_OrgUnit
- PA_CD_Person
- PA_CD_ReferenceData
- PA_CD_Reports_Daily
- PA_CD_Reports_Monthly

1. Create a new machine group in AutoSys containing the below servers:
EPRIAPP225SA
EPRIAPP225SB
EPRIAPP225SC
EPRIAPP225SD

2. NOTIFY REQUESTOR BEFORE IMPLEMENTING THIS STEP
Assign the server EPRIAPP225SA to the batch job PA_CD_ReferenceData and force start the job. Requestor will monitor the job to check for failures. If the run is unsuccessful, revert PA_CD_ReferenceData to run on the old server cluster again.

3. If the test in step 2 was successful, assign the new machine group to all CD batch jobs. Requestor will monitor jobs to check for failures. If any unsuccessful runs are found, batch jobs will need to be reverted back to the old servers.

short_description: Minister Rishworth Micro PC Incident Report
description:
Hi Kathleen,
I'm from the Workplace Systems team at DEWR. We have been working with Premier Support on investigating the incident involving the Minister's Micro PC in Adelaide on 19 June.

As requested, please find below a summary of our findings and actions taken.

Thank you for your patience with this request. Due to the technical nature of the issue presented it has taken some time to vet the log files provided.  The Premier Support team will reach out to work closely with you in support of the recommended next steps.

Background

1.      On Friday 19 June, the Minister's office reported that the Minister's account had been locked, preventing ability to login.

2.      During troubleshooting, it was identified that the associated Micro PC had lost its trust relationship with Active Directory, preventing normal authentication.

Action taken to resolve the issue

3.      The device was manually reconnected to the domain to re-establish its trust relationship with the Active Directory.

4.      Support was provided to the Minister in relation to Windows Hello (pin or face id sign in method) which was separate to the issue impacting the Micro PC.

Investigation findings

5.      This is the second occurrence of a similar issue affecting the Minister's device, with a previous incident involving device DA336986 on 4 December 2025.

6.      While the symptom is consistent across both incidents - namely, a domain trust failure - the contributing circumstances may not be the same.

7.      Investigation of diagnostic logs has identified a time synchronisation issue, which can cause secure connection failure and breakdown of the computer trust relationship, preventing successful domain authentication.

Recommended next steps

8.      Replace the device as a priority with a newer model device and further investigate the current device.

9.      Prior to deployment of this device, assurance activities on the replacement device will be undertaken including ensuring it is successfully joined to the network and date and time are synchronising.

10.  Measures are put in place to proactively monitor the Minister's device health to ensure the domain connection remains stable.


Kind regards,
